1149: How to read "liquid+liquid" and "B2+B2". A segment in which the same phase name appears twice is a locally convex-upward part of a single G(x) curve that the lower convex hull of stage 06 picked up as "coexistence of the same phase at compositions x_a and x_b" (which is exactly the miscibility-gap criterion). The liquid is fitted as one curve, ideal mixing + 4-term Redlich–Kister, through the calphy results at 11 compositions; no alternative liquid models were compared. A real gap would move its boundaries under the Monte Carlo error propagation, but here they stay fixed with standard deviation 0, so they are judged to be curvature that the fit followed from the 1–2 meV/atom noise of the samples. REPORT.md lists them separately as "Same-phase segments". Treat them as physics only if the width exceeds 0.1 and they survive adding composition points. The B2+B2 of Ni–Al stage 3 was caused by the cusp of the sublattice model and disappeared with the thermal-defect model of stage 4 (section 5).
1150: With a single GPU the jobs run serially, so the total throughput is about the same as 8 CPU cores (4 ranks × 2 jobs concurrently). The benefits are a shorter wait per job and freeing the CPUs for QHA. calphy returns an error of 0 with n_iterations: 1, so in practice use 3 or more iterations and pass G_err to sensitivity.
